name: HubSpot
use_case: read and update contacts, companies and deals in customers' HubSpot portals

verdict.label: Hard · weeks of waiting
verdict.summary: Building is self-serve, but an unlisted app stops at 25 installs. Customer 26 just can't install it. Getting past that means a marketplace listing, which needs real installs first and a review HubSpot says should wrap up within 60 days of their feedback.
verdict.active_effort: 1–2 hours (CLI project setup); 1–2 days for the listing
verdict.wait: None for your first 25 installs; listing review up to ~60 days
verdict.gating_step: The 25-install cap until your HubSpot Marketplace listing is approved

concept: On HubSpot's current developer platform (2025.2+), an app is a project you create and upload with the HubSpot CLI. Its OAuth settings (redirect URLs, scopes) live in app-hsmeta.json. Each customer portal that installs the app grants your integration a token for that portal. The app's distribution type decides how many portals can install it.

paths.name: Pilot (up to 25 accounts)
paths.when: Early customers. Marketplace-distribution OAuth app, unlisted.

paths.name: AI connector listing
paths.when: Your app mainly connects HubSpot to generative-AI tools. Extra rules: user-level permissions and built on HubSpot's MCP Server.

composio.managed_note: Composio's HubSpot toolkit lists a Composio-managed OAuth app (OAuth2; API key is also supported).
when_own_app: Production: users should see your app name on the consent screen, not “Composio”.
You need scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
You need your own rate-limit quota (managed apps share quota across Composio users).
You need faster polling triggers than the managed 15-minute minimum.
Self-hosted or regional instances of the provider.

stages.name: Build & test (works today, up to 25 installs)
stages.summary: Configuration is code: you edit JSON in a project and upload it with the CLI rather than clicking through a form.

limits.text: A Marketplace-distribution OAuth app can be installed in up to 25 accounts before it's listed (developer test accounts don't count). Enforced since September 22, 2025.

steps.title: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Run `hs account auth` against your developer account. HubSpot's guide recommends CLI v7.6.0 or later.

steps.title: Create the project: `hs project create` → App
steps.detail: Choose distribution “marketplace” and authentication “OAuth”. Static-token apps can't serve other customers' portals.

steps.title: Set redirect URLs and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Put Composio's callback URL in config.auth.redirectUrls. Split scopes into requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes.

steps.title: Upload: `hs project upload`
steps.detail: Then run `hs project open` → your app → Auth tab to copy the Client ID and secret into Composio.

steps.title: Install into a developer test account
steps.detail: Developer test accounts don't count toward the 25-install cap, so test there. Installing in a standard account requires a user with the right permissions, such as a super admin.

stages.name: Go to production (HubSpot Marketplace listing)
stages.summary: Listing removes the cap. Treat it as a launch project, because HubSpot reviews listing quality closely.

limits.text: Only one app can be submitted for approval at a time; extra submissions are rejected automatically.

steps.title: Get real installs first
steps.detail: Submitting a listing currently needs a minimum of active installs in unaffiliated production accounts. Third-party sources cite 3, and HubSpot has changed this threshold before.

steps.title: Make every listing URL live and accurate
steps.detail: HubSpot crawls them. Pricing must match your website, and the shared-data section must match the scopes you request.

steps.title: If you're an AI connector, meet the extra rules
steps.detail: Use user-level permissions and build on HubSpot's MCP Server.

steps.title: Submit the listing and work through feedback
steps.detail: HubSpot says the review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared. After approval, the install cap is lifted.

requirements.detail: Apps on the current platform are created as CLI projects.

requirements.item: OAuth as the only auth method
requirements.detail: Marketplace apps must be public OAuth apps.

requirements.item: Live, crawlable listing URLs and matching pricing
requirements.detail: Privacy policy, support and install links included.

gotchas.title: Customer #26 can't install
gotchas.detail: Teams have hit the cap in production with no warning in the UI. HubSpot community moderators say it isn't waived; listing approval is the way out.

gotchas.title: Migrating a legacy app applies the cap
gotchas.detail: Moving an older public app with more than 25 installs onto the new platform enforces the limit automatically.

gotchas.title: Unlisted apps show an unverified warning
gotchas.detail: Users connecting an unlisted app can see an “App not reviewed by HubSpot” style warning.

gotchas.title: Broken listing links send you back to draft
gotchas.detail: Unreachable privacy, support or install links are a common reason listings get returned.

blockers.symptom: “App install limit” error for a new customer
blockers.fix: Get the Marketplace listing approved; developer test accounts don't count, so keep testing there.

blockers.cause: The callback URL isn't in config.auth.redirectUrls of the uploaded project.
blockers.fix: Add Composio's callback URL, run `hs project upload` again, and retry.

blockers.cause: Usually unreachable listing URLs or incomplete fields.
blockers.fix: Fix links and content, then resubmit.

agent: Scaffold the CLI project and write app-hsmeta.json
Map tools to required vs optional scopes
Draft the listing copy, shared-data table and setup docs
you: Create the developer account and authenticate the CLI
Submit the listing and handle reviewer feedback

uncertainties: The minimum active-install requirement for listing (3) comes from a partner agency's write-up; HubSpot's page should be checked at submission time.
How long reviews take before the first feedback arrives isn't stated; the 60-day figure counts from when feedback is shared.
